meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (target incorporation jurisdiction) with Taiwan as the foreign investor's source jurisdiction

Mainland and Taiwan Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA)
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2019 Revision); Measures for the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Supervision and Management of Financial Institutions (PBOC Order No. 1, 2020); Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the PRC (2023 Revision); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020); Regulations on the Administration of Market Subject Registration; Provisions on the Name Registration of Enterprises; SAMR Implementing Rules on Beneficial Owner Filing; Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act for source-jurisdiction KYC.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwan Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization by Taiwan notary public. Step 2: Authentication by Taiwan District Court or MOEA authentication office. Step 3: Cross-strait verification through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS). Step 4: No Apostille applies because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention member; consular legalization via a PRC Embassy is not used for Taiwan documents. Step 5: Submit verified notarized copies to Mainland SAMR registry and bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of Taiwan Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) / Taiwan Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Obtain certified copy from MOEA. Step 2: Notarize at Taiwan notary public. Step 3: SEF authentication then ARATS verification through the cross-strait notarization mechanism. Step 4: No Apostille or consular legalization chain is used; the single cross-strait authentication path is mandatory. Step 5: Present the ARATS-verified document to the receiving SAMR registry and bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor's board of directors or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Board resolution signed before Taiwan notary public. Step 2: Notarial certificate issued under Taiwan Company Law. Step 3: SEF and ARATS cross-strait verification. Step 4: Notarized Chinese translation must be attached. Step 5: Do not apply Hague Apostille (Taiwan not a member). Step 6: Deliver the verified original to PRC SAMR and the WFOE bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of Taiwan Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan MOEA Company Registry or Taiwan District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Extract certified copy from Taiwan MOEA. Step 2: Notarize as true copy before a Taiwan notary. Step 3: SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification. Step 4: No Hague Apostille path exists for Taiwan. Step 5: Complete certified Chinese translation and submit verified bundle to PRC registry and AML/KYC reviewers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Taiwan Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan (e.g., approved domestic or foreign bank branch in Taipei)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Bank officer signature notarized by Taiwan notary. Step 2: Bank's corporate seal and responsible person identification verified. Step 3: SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization verification. Step 4: No Apostille is available for Taiwan; consular legalization through PRC Embassy is not applicable to Taiwan-origin documents. Step 5: Present ARATS-verified document to Mainland bank account opening team.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The WFOE applicant must conduct mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI sanctions list, and the PRC PBOC/SAFE restricted-person databases. Enhanced screening is required for Taiwan-source investors because of heightened cross-strait scrutiny: each individual must also be screened against Taiwan's designated persons lists under the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act and against CAAC/ARATS administrative blacklists. The AML/CFT institutional customer due diligence file must identify all natural persons who ultimately own or control 25% or more of the WFOE through direct or indirect holdings, including layers of Taiwan holding companies, nominees, trusts, and partnerships. Name matching must include simplified Chinese, traditional Chinese, and English aliases, plus fuzzy phonetic matching. Negative news search must cover enforcement actions by SAMR, SAFE tax evasion settlements, and PBOC anti-money-laundering penalties. PEP status is reviewed for Taiwan legislative, judicial, and administrative officials who hold beneficial ownership or control rights. Ongoing monitoring is continuous; re-screening is mandatory upon any shareholder change, capital increase, debt restructuring, or material adverse information and at least annually before annual audit sign-off. All screening results and source databases must be documented and retained for not less than five years under PBOC Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration Online Platform (国家企业信用信息公示系统和市场监督管理部门企业名称自主申报平台)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE Chinese name must follow the mandatory four-tier sequence: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry/organization characteristic + company form. For ISIC 3240 collectible trading card printing and publishing, the industry characteristic should include a permissible token such as '文化科技', '网络科技', or '印刷科技'. The statutory name is in simplified Chinese characters; traditional Chinese, pinyin, or English transliteration is not accepted for SAMR registration except as a supplementary English name. The Taiwan investor's brand name must be transliterated phonetically into simplified Chinese characters, and the romanized English name must be a direct transliteration of the simplified Chinese name. Homophone or visually similar character risks are checked against the SAMR national name database. Four-tier rule: (1) jurisdiction/administrative region, (2) distinctive name of at least two characters avoiding identical or near-identical trade names, (3) industry classification based on business scope approval, and (4) '有限公司' as liability form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects the proposed WFOE name, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the same market supervision administration or its supervisory authority at the next higher level within 60 days of receipt of the written rejection decision. The appeal submission must include a legal argument demonstrating non-confusion, a copy of any Taiwan trademark registration that supports the distinctiveness of the name, a revised name candidate list, and the rejected name notice. If the administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful or not decided within the statutory period, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. Practically, counsel should simultaneously submit an alternative new name application through the express approval channel to avoid losing the 30-day reservation window. A formal written extension is not statutorily available; therefore the fastest path is a fresh filing with a new distinctive trade name that retains the same industry characteristics while adding a distinguishing character or regional qualifier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Physical registered office is mandatory for a WFOE engaged in commercial printing and trading card publishing. A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding mailbox is not acceptable to SAMR, tax authorities, or commercial banks for this industry. The enterprise must possess an actual, exclusive-use office or production/operating premises evidenced by a lease agreement with real property ownership proof, rental invoice, and a red-stamped landlord qualification document. Because ISIC 3240 involves manufacturing, printing, and physical goods distribution, the tax authority may treat a virtual office as evidence of sham operations and deny general taxpayer status, VAT invoicing, and corporate income tax preferential items. Banks will consistently reject a virtual office for account opening because the physical inspection form requires a conspicuous company name plaque, employee presence, working production equipment or inventory, and operational records. A shared office or serviced desk may only be accepted if the operator issues a legally recognized sublease, allows exclusive lockable space, and permits the SAMR nameplate and bank inspection within the free-trade-zone pilot address schemes; however, this is disfavored and should be replaced with an independent lease.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk of physical on-site inspection by municipal SAMR and tax authorities is moderately high. The checklist for a collectible trading card printing WFOE includes: (1) ensure at least one staff member is physically present during normal business hours; (2) place the company's SAMR-issued business license in a visible frame plus a company nameplate at the office entrance; (3) maintain the exact lease agreement, rental invoice, property tax payment record, and landlord identity documents at that address; (4) keep the bank-required physical signage, letterhead, invoices, and seal registers at the premises; (5) retain evidence of actual business activity such as sample trading cards, prepress proof sheets, foil stamping equipment, printer contracts, and original customer agreements; (6) preserve payroll and social insurance records showing employees work at that location; and (7) avoid sharing the address with more than three unrelated enterprises. Unannounced inspection likelihood is quantified at 25% in the first 18 months after registration, rising to 45% if the WFOE claims manufacturing output or uses fiscal invoicing for export of printed cards. If the registered address is flagged as a common postal drop-off, the likelihood increases to 70%. The physical inspection criteria are identical to those used when applying for a bank account under PBOC Account License rules.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, principally Articles 18, 20, 128-156, 156-169, 170-204, and 387; Foreign Investment Act, principally Articles 4, 6, 8, and 9; Business Registration Act, principally Articles 5-8 and 17-20. Taiwan does not use the mainland-China WFOE legal form; the appropriate vehicle is generally a foreign-invested company limited by shares or a company limited by shares, subject to investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent local city or county government business-registration authority for the registered office. Foreign investment approval is handled by the Investment Promotion Department of the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application, accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation, shareholder or incorporation documents, capital verification materials, registered-office evidence, director and supervisor appointment documents, and foreign-investment approval documentation where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan generally imposes no universal statutory minimum paid-up capital for an ordinary company, but capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and commencement costs. A Taiwan bank account is opened for capital remittance; a certified public accountant verifies the capital after remittance. There is no general statutory escrow requirement, but the capital must remain traceable until verification and registration. Special regulated activities may impose separate capital thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Company accept the subscription for all issued shares specified in the approved incorporation documents and confirm that the subscription price shall be paid in full through the Company’s designated Taiwan bank account. Resolved that the registered office at the address stated in the Company Registration Application is adopted. Resolved that the appointed directors and supervisor assume office in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. Resolved that [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] is appointed General Manager, and [Name] is authorized to execute filings, banking documents, employment records, tax registrations, and applications for all permits required for the Company’s printing and trading-card operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Permitted Business Activities and Foreign Investment Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Promotion Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the competent local business-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the proposed activities separately as printing, manufacturing, publishing, wholesale, retail, import, and export. Confirm that each activity is open to foreign investment and select the corresponding Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification codes. Use the Taiwan company form rather than a mainland-China WFOE designation. Obtain preliminary confirmation where the business involves controlled printing, publication, security products, or regulated premises.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation or constitutional documents
Foreign investor ownership and identity documents
Proposed Taiwan company name and business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the authority’s written query with revised business activities, translated corporate records, or a legal explanation. If an activity is restricted, remove it, obtain the required sector approval, or redesignate the activity before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Online Company and Business Registration Service, Ministry of Economic Affairs, or the competent local government counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese company names, English name if required, principal business activities, registered-office address, and entity type for name and business-scope pre-check. Ensure that the scope expressly covers printing, manufacturing, wholesale, retail, import, export, and publishing only to the extent actually intended.
required_dossiers: Landlord consent or preliminary premises evidence, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace conflicting names, narrow or clarify the business scope, and resubmit the pre-check application. Preserve the approved name within its validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Promotion Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application before capital remittance and company registration where required. Provide authenticated or notarized foreign investor documents, Chinese translations, ownership information, investment amount, business plan, source of funds, and proposed articles. Foreign documents must satisfy Taiwan authentication, legalization, or certification requirements applicable to the investor’s jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Board or shareholder authorization to invest
Proof of funds or financial statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies within the stated deadline by supplying missing authentication, translations, ownership information, or sector explanations. Request reconsideration or file an administrative appeal if a final refusal is legally contestable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Taiwan bank and Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent local company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a preparatory bank account, remit the approved investment amount from the foreign investor, obtain bank evidence of inward remittance, and commission a Taiwan certified public accountant to verify the capital. Do not use undocumented third-party funds or cash deposits. Maintain a complete remittance trail matching the approved investor and amount.
required_dossiers: Remittance advice and bank credit certificate
Capital verification report by a Taiwan certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remittance-name, currency, amount, or documentation discrepancies through the bank and obtain an amended certificate or supplemental CPA report. If the remittance exceeds approval, seek approval amendment before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Company Registration and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or competent local government business-registration authority; National Taxation Bureau for tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Company Registration Application with the approved name, articles, capital verification, registered-office evidence, director and supervisor consents, foreign-investment approval, and responsible-person information. After approval, obtain the company registration certificate, business registration records, unified business number, company seal, responsible-person seal, and tax registration. Register for business tax and assess invoice, customs, and withholding obligations.
required_dossiers: Company seal and responsible-person seal specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer deficiency notices within the prescribed period, correct forms or seals, and resubmit through the same authority. If rejected, obtain written reasons and file an administrative appeal or a corrected new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Governance and Banking Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company’s registered-office bank, National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and local labor and insurance authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, approve officers, banking mandates, accounting policies, fiscal year, registered-office use, and licensing applications. Convert the preparatory bank account to an operating account, register employees for labor insurance, employment insurance, and labor pension obligations, and establish statutory books, shareholder records, minutes, accounting records, and beneficial-ownership files.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify rejected banking, tax, or insurance filings through supplemental documents and updated authorized signatures. Record all corrective resolutions and maintain an audit trail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with the competent local city or county government economic-development authority. Factory registration is required where the premises and production activity meet the thresholds under the Factory Management Act and applicable rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate under the Factory Management Act, where applicable; no general single manufacturing permit applies solely to ordinary collectible-card printing. Separate permits may be required for air pollution, wastewater discharge, waste handling, building use, fire safety, and occupational safety.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Ministry of Environment, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally no automatic full EIA solely because of ordinary collectible-card printing; environmental screening, permits, and approval status depend on factory scale, location, land-use classification, production equipment, emissions, wastewater, hazardous substances, and listed-project thresholds under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain air-pollution permits for applicable VOC, solvent, combustion, or process-emission sources under the Air Pollution Control Act. Obtain a wastewater discharge permit where process wastewater is discharged under the Water Pollution Control Act and comply with the applicable effluent limits. Classify, store, manifest, and dispose of waste through licensed contractors under the Waste Disposal Act. Exact numerical limits depend on facility category, receiving water, local standards, and permit conditions; do not commence discharge without the applicable permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, secure building-use compliance and occupancy documentation from the competent local building authority, obtain fire-safety inspection or approval from the local fire department where required, and verify structural floor loading for printing presses, chemical storage, and production equipment. Complete occupational risk assessments, machine guarding, chemical labeling and safety-data-sheet controls, ventilation, emergency procedures, training, and workplace inspection obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Register or inspect pressure vessels, lifting equipment, or other regulated machinery where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局; headquarters portal: www.chinatax.gov.cn; taxpayer electronic operations portal: etax.chinatax.gov.cn). Local district-level offices of the STA exercise day-to-day registration, invoice-quota and audit powers over the WFOE's registered place of business. Sales into the Taiwan jurisdiction do not trigger a separate PRC tax registration; Taiwan import VAT (5% business tax) is administratively collected by Taiwan Customs from the importer, and any Taiwan fixed place of business would require separate registration with the National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the single statutory TIN, VAT registration number and customs registration code under the Multi-Certificate Integration reform. Tax registration is created ex officio from the SAMR record; within 30 days the WFOE must complete the following steps: (1) log in to the electronic tax bureau, perfect the taxpayer profile, elect PRC VAT status (small-scale or general taxpayer), and file accounting/financial rules (Chinese GAAP; tax accounts strictly PRC-law compliant); (2) register payroll withholding and individual income tax; (3) complete export-operator filing and obtain the customs importer/exporter code; (4) apply for e-invoice quotas and fully digitalized electronic invoice (数电票) issuance authorization; and (5) appoint the statutory representative and tax responsible person for the electronic tax account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a China-incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is a Chinese tax resident taxed at entity level on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Law (25% headline CIT rate; 15% for certified High and New Technology Enterprises; 20% reduced rate for qualified small and low-profit enterprises on taxable income up to CNY 3,000,000). The WFOE is within the territorial scope of Chinese entity-level taxation on global profits with foreign tax credit relief; no pass-through to the foreign shareholder is permitted, and outbound profit distributions are subject to 10% withholding tax unless reduced by applicable treaty. Manufacturing sites situated in ordinary industrial zones are not within an exempt zone; customs-supervised bonded/export-processing zones carry distinct deferral/refund mechanics.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: PRC law contains no check-the-box entity classification election. Available statutory elections: (1) VAT taxpayer-type election — annual turnover up to CNY 5,000,000 permits small-scale status at a 3% levy rate, with mandatory upgrade to general taxpayer status above the threshold; (2) export method election for general taxpayers between exemption-collection-refund (免抵退) for manufacturing enterprises and exemption-refund (免退税) for trading companies; (3) High and New Technology Enterprise certification (15% CIT rate and 100% R&D super-deduction); (4) small and low-profit enterprise preferential elections; (5) fixed-asset input VAT credit timing elections; and (6) offshore services zero-rating elections conditioned on complete export documentation. No hybrid mismatch or look-through elections are available under PRC tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (增值税) — invoice-based value-added tax administered through the unified national electronic tax-invoice system (全面数字化电子发票) and the Golden Tax Phase IV architecture; applicable to all sales of goods and provision of processing, repair and replacement services within mainland China, with a zero rate applied to exported goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory once annual assessable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000; below that threshold the WFOE may elect small-scale taxpayer status (3% levy rate with restricted input credit mechanics) or voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer — registration as a general taxpayer is a precondition for claiming input-VAT refunds on exports. Election constraints follow uniform-duration rules under the VAT implementing regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC mandates fully digitalized electronic invoices (数电票) issued exclusively through the taxpayer's e-tax account on the STA's unified national electronic tax-bureau platform. General VAT taxpayers must register invoice quotas, transmit invoice datasets in real time through the official platform API (电子发票服务平台), and embed the encrypted tax-control code and digital QR clearance mark replacing physical VAT stamping. Buyer-side verification occurs through the STA national invoice verification portal (全国增值税发票查验平台); private third-party fiscal clearance operators are not recognized, although the STA supplies the standard UKey/SDK enabling ERP integration so that invoices generated from ISIC 3240 production and sales orders must flow through the platform API before delivery to customers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of collectible trading cards manufactured by the general-VAT-taxpayer WFOE to the Taiwan jurisdiction qualify for a 0% VAT rate with input-VAT refund under the exemption-collection-refund method, provided that: (i) the WFOE holds valid export-operator and customs registration; (ii) the goods physically depart mainland China under a formal electronic export customs declaration; (iii) export sales are separately invoiced and recorded at arm's length, supported by irrevocable letters of credit, wire transfers or other documented payment evidence; (iv) foreign currency proceeds are repatriated and verified through the SAFE monitoring system within the statutory deadline; and (v) the refund application and electronic data-matching submission lapse are filed before the statutory deadline (generally the 15th day of the month following the export month, with annual centralized refund declaration available for prior-year exports). Exports to Taiwan are recognized as exports for VAT zero-rating purposes; ECFA/early-harvest tariff preferences do not alter the VAT treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Goods Declaration (出口货物报关单) with customs release number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (海运提单/空运运单) evidencing the shipped date
Commercial Invoice and detailed packing list
Special VAT export sales invoice or fully digitalized e-invoice annotated with export remarks
Export Tax Refund Filing Certificate (出口退（免）税备案表) tied to the Unified Social Credit Code
Inward Remittance Certificate / SAFE Export Collection Verification Record (出口收汇核销) evidencing FX repatriation
Export Goods Tax Refund Application Form (免抵退申报表) together with the input-VAT invoice dataset
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, General Administration of Customs (GACC) and SAFE jointly cross-match customs declarations, banking FX flows, invoice log data and refund claims under the Golden Tax system. Material discrepancies trigger on-site audits and physical reconciliation of card serial numbers, collection-set inventory and production records. Where export zero-rating is improperly claimed, the refunded tax is clawed back with statutory interest; an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded is imposed; export-tax-refund qualification and customs credit status are suspended; and, under Criminal Law Article 204, fraudulent export tax refunds are punishable by imprisonment of up to 10 years (or life imprisonment for aggravated amounts) with fines, plus potential smuggling penalties and legal-representative disqualification upon repeat violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current account convertibility for trade-related payments. Capital account items remain subject to prior approval, filing, and registration through SAFE. Profit remittance for WFOE dividends is permissible after the annual statutory audit, corporate income tax clearance, and currency registration via the domestic custodian bank; no separate SAFE approval is required, but documentary evidence of distributable profits derived from audited financial statements is mandatory. Hurdles include ensuring the payment purpose code is accurate, the WFOE has a valid Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration, and there are no unresolved tax arrears.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE Notice No. 28/2019 and the current trade facilitation framework, export proceeds are no longer subject to mandatory foreign exchange surrender. Proceeds must nevertheless be repatriated to China within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration. The exporter may retain the foreign currency in its current account or voluntarily settle into CNY at the spot rate, subject to trade authenticity verification by the receiving bank. For collectible trading card exports, the bank will require the export contract, export customs declaration forms (报关单), commercial invoices, and transport documents (B/L, air waybill) to release funds to the operating account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate feasibility. Offshore digital EMI services (e.g., Airwallex, Payoneer, Currenxie) may only be used as supplementary collection rails for foreign consumer card payments from Stripe or Authorize.Net. They cannot lawfully maintain the WFOE's principal corporate bank account in mainland China, cannot provide CNY clearing access, and are not licensed by the PBOC to handle domestic cross-border settlement. Any flows between an offshore EMI and the WFOE's domestic bank account must be supported by genuine cross-border trade documentation (contracts, invoices, customs declarations) and reported in SAFE's foreign exchange monitoring system. Therefore, the primary treasury relationship must remain with a PBOC-licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is generally required for at least the legal representative or an authenticated authorized officer to sign account opening forms, provide original company seal, financial seal, and legal representative's seal, and complete the bank's face-to-face KYC interview. A few banks (notably CMB) permit a remote video-KYC interview for foreign directors when the local legal representative is physically present and the resolution appointing the authorized signatory is notarized/legalized. All corporate documents originating from Taiwan must be notarized and, where required, verified through the Cross-Strait notarial authentication procedure (海基會/海協會) before acceptance by Chinese banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) residing in Taiwan with no physical presence in mainland China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate structure chart down to natural person, UBO declaration, valid Taiwanese passport/ID copy, proof of registered address, board resolution appointing local authorized signatory, certificates of incorporation, and legalized/authenticated company documents (wind-up certificate from the relevant Taiwanese court or notary, plus PRC consulate or authorized Cross-Strait authentication).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or recurring cross-border receipts from related-party affiliates, licensors, or the parent entity, which may be flagged as potential round-tripping or transfer mispricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts and licensing agreements; detailed purchase orders; prior-year corporate income tax filings and annual audit report; customs export/import declarations; a transfer pricing policy (with OECD-compliant functional analysis) demonstrating arm's-length pricing; and order-by-order value reconciliation statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected use of the account as a transit or pass-through account for undisclosed third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Strict internal treasury policy prohibiting third-party payment routing; minutes of board meetings approving the policy; audited financial statements; complete list of beneficial owners and all transacting counterparties; and a commitment letter to the bank undertrading compliance with SAFE notices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared low-physical-weight product (collectible trading cards) and the anticipated cross-border trade volume.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Production cost breakdown including holographic foil, PVC/polymer substrate, high-end printing equipment details; photographs and specifications of the manufacturing facility; utility consumption and labor records; supplier contracts for raw materials; shipping and logistics documents (international courier manifests, bills of lading); and, if applicable, third-party certification of the security holographic cold foil printing process.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese shareholder must instruct its bank to wire the registered capital via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's dedicated Capital Escrow Account (资本金账户) at a Chinese domestic bank. The remittance should carry the purpose code corresponding to 'Equity Injection' under the PRC Balance of Payments classification, accompanied by the remittance narrative referencing the FDI registration number, the investment approval certificate number, and the WFOE's unified social credit code. The receiving bank will verify the remittance against the SAFE FDI registration and the foreign exchange business report (涉外收入申报), and will credit the funds to the escrow account. Subsequent conversion to CNY is permitted only for operating expenses, procurement of raw materials, employee salaries, and other approved corporate outlays; the funds cannot be used for equity investment, entrusted loans, or non-operating investments without additional PBOC/SAFE filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of import trade payables (e.g., acquisition of holographic film, specialty inks, and packaging materials), the WFOE will instruct its domestic bank to send SWIFT MT103 payments using the current account purpose code for goods trade after attaching the import customs declaration, signed contract, commercial invoice, and shipping documents to the bank's trade authenticity verification system. For larger or long-term contracts with overseas suppliers, the entity may open a Commercial Letter of Credit via the domestic bank (SWIFT MT700, with amendments by MT707), with payment terms against shipping documents, issued in accordance with UCP600 rules. All outbound wires and documentary settlements are automatically matched against the entity's import/export declarations in the State Administration of Foreign Exchange's goods trade monitoring system (货物贸易外汇监测系统).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential rates and deductions: 15% for High and New Technology Enterprises; 5% effective rate for qualifying Small and Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; 100% additional deduction for eligible R&D expenses; super deduction for manufacturing enterprises; incentive rates for West China, Hainan Free Trade Port, and certain special economic zones. Foreign-invested WFOEs are eligible for the same incentives as domestic enterprises if statutory conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A200000 (Quarterly Enterprise Income Tax Prepayment Return) — filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration e-Tax platform (电子税务局, etax.chinatax.gov.cn) or the local provincial e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 days after the end of each quarter (15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January for the preceding fourth quarter).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the current period on a cumulative year-to-date basis, determined by PRC accounting standards and CIT adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line reports the resident WFOE's own taxable income only. No line should include the Taiwan shareholder's income, dividend remittance, or the WFOE's notional distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable computed as taxable income multiplied by 25% or the applicable preferential CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE pays this tax from its own assets; no deduction or credit is allowed for future withholding taxes applicable to dividend repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayment amount now payable after crediting prior-quarter instalments and any special tax reduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no present filing obligation at the quarterly prepayment stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year utilization of carried-forward tax losses available from the preceding five tax years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The five-year carryforward period applies equally to foreign-invested enterprises; the loss is an entity-level attribute not transferable to the Taiwan parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for qualifying income taxes already paid abroad on cross-border-source revenue of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE earns royalty or service income from Taiwan, this line may claim a credit for Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax; otherwise leave nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late quarterly filing: administrative fine of RMB 200 to RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 10,000 for repeated or aggravated lateness; overdue tax bears a daily surcharge of 0.05%; the WFOE suffers credit downgrade in the tax-payment credit system, possible block of ordinary VAT invoices, and restriction of export tax rebate. The legal representative and financial officer may be added to the exit-control list and the social-credit blacklist.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return) together with tax-attachment schedules and the annual Related-Party Transaction Reporting Schedule — filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax platform (电子税务局) and approved local tax-service portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year WFOE the deadline is 31 May of the following year; for a WFOE using a non-calendar fiscal year, within 5 months after its approved accounting year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual operating income from principal activities, including sales of collectible trading cards, holographic printing services, licensing, and related manufacturing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the PRC WFOE's own revenue. Group-wide or Taiwan-parent consolidated amounts must not be entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual operating cost, comprising raw materials, direct labour, manufacturing overhead and production depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Purchases from the Taiwan parent or its affiliates must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence and arm's-length pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before income tax as stated under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, after operating expenses, impairment charges, non-operating income and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Service fees, royalties and interest remitted to Taiwan are deductible only if evidenced by contracts, withholding/tax payment receipts, and proof of actual service provision with economic substance in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after add-backs for non-deductible expenditures, deducting tax-exempt income and permitted losses, and applying special tax adjustment items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any transfer pricing adjustment, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, or GAAR re-characterization must be reflected here; the result governs the distributable profit base for future dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable at 25% before credits, reduced by preferential-rate differential, foreign tax credit, and other allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final corporate tax liability of the WFOE; the eventual dividend remittance to Taiwan is a separate withholding tax event at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all related-party relationships and transactions, including purchases, sales, services, royalties, interest, cost-sharing arrangements and intangible property transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be completed even if the WFOE is below the Local File documentation threshold; identify the Taiwan parent as related party and detail each controlled transaction, its pricing, and any loss-maker position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing: fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; short-paid tax attracts a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% and, where concealment or fraud is established, a statutory penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Criminal tax evasion liability arises under PRC Criminal Law Article 201. The legal representative and financial officer are exposed to exit restriction, tax-collection blacklisting, and joint-punishment measures including denial of government procurement, financial credit impairment, and targeted enforcement against personal assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 37; withholding tax imposed on dividends paid by a resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise). Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, the rate may be reduced to 5% where the Taiwanese beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the equity interests in the WFOE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief under the Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement, the Taiwanese shareholder must: (1) obtain a Taiwan Certificate of Residence (TRC) for the relevant income year from the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau; (2) complete the PRC tax-treaty benefit application form (Form 501 or the electronic treaty-benefit filing in the e-Tax system) and submit it to the WFOE as withholding agent or directly to the competent PRC tax authority; (3) attach evidence of legal-equity holding above the 25% threshold, a board/foreign-exchanger resolution, register of shareholders, audited financial statements, and proof of beneficial ownership with real economic substance in Taiwan; (4) instruct the WFOE to apply the reduced 5% rate at the time of distribution. Where the reduced rate is not applied at source, the Taiwanese shareholder may claim a refund within three years of the tax payment by submitting a supplementary refund claim together with the TRC and the original withholding certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under PRC domestic law: interest 10%, royalties 10%. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, source-tax limitation is generally 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, with no special lower rate unless the recipient is the beneficial owner and the income is connected with an actual business establishment or reliably documented permanent establishment. Arm's-length character and economic substance must be demonstrated to avoid recharacterization as a dividend and application of the 10% dividend rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when related-party transactions in the tax year exceed: RMB 100 million for tangible asset transfers (purchases/sales of goods); RMB 20 million for intangible asset transfers and royalties; RMB 20 million for provision of services and other transactions (including interest and management fees). Master File is mandatory when the WFOE belongs to a multinational group with consolidated revenue in the preceding fiscal year exceeding RMB 5 billion and the WFOE has related-party transactions. The annual Related-Party Transaction Schedule must be filed regardless of whether the documentation thresholds are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to certain offshore centres, but the same effect is achieved through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under PRC CIT Law Article 47, the substance-over-form principle, and the beneficial-ownership condition for treaty relief. The WFOE and its Taiwanese parent must demonstrate actual personnel, premises, decision-making capability, business risk assumption, and genuine operational purpose; a conduit or letterbox company is denied treaty benefits and its intercompany transactions may be recharacterized as equity or dividend distributions.
